name: schema-annotation-invalid
description: An annotation attribute value does not follow the prefix:id value grammar or cites a source that has no row in the Sources section.
common_causes: A prefix was used in an annotation value but no row for it was added to the Prefixes section
The property part of the value was misspelled or was never added to the External annotations section
An external term such as foodonto:FOODON_00001234 was written bare instead of as the value of a mapping property
A dc:source value cites a source whose name has no row in the Sources section
A dc:source value cites a URL that is not under the link of any Sources row
The value of skos:exactMatch or skos:closeMatch was written as a bare identifier or a URL instead of in prefix notation
explanation: The value of an annotation attribute has the form 'prefix:id value': 'prefix:id' names a row of the External annotations section, whose 'prefix' is a row of the Prefixes section, and 'value' is that property's value. A link from a schema element to a term in an external ontology is written with a SKOS mapping property whose value is the external term in prefix notation, as in 'skos:exactMatch ncit:C25499' for the same concept or 'skos:closeMatch ncit:C25499' for one close enough to be used interchangeably in most applications; the prefix of that term must also be a row of the Prefixes section, while the term itself is not checked. A 'dc:source' value must name a row of the Sources section: the text either begins with a row's 'source' name or contains a URL that begins with a row's 'link' (compared without the scheme and without a trailing slash), and any other text such as 'Adapted from' is free. Four situations are flagged: (a) the prefix of the value is not a Prefixes row; (b) the 'prefix:id' is not an External annotations row, which is where a bare external term falls; (c) a 'dc:source' value names no Sources row; (d) the value of a mapping property has the form 'prefix:term' but its prefix is not a Prefixes row, or a mapping property's value is not in prefix notation at all. Every one of these is a warning and the schema still loads. The rows of a partnered library's standard schema count as the library's own, so a library partnered with the standard schema may use the standard's prefixes, external annotations, and sources without repeating them. The rules apply to standard schemas with versions 8.5.0 or later and to library schemas partnered with them; earlier schemas wrote bare external terms and are not checked.
correction_strategy: Write every annotation value as 'prefix:id value' with the prefix in the Prefixes section and the 'prefix:id' in the External annotations section, link an external term with skos:exactMatch or skos:closeMatch followed by the term in prefix notation, and make every dc:source value begin with a Sources row name or contain a URL under a Sources row link

correction_examples.explanation: Reason a: the prefix 'nowhere:' had no row in the Prefixes section; a defined prefix was used instead
Reason b: a bare external term is not an External annotations row; the term becomes the value of a SKOS mapping property
Reason c: the dc:source text named no Sources row; it now begins with the 'source' name of one
Reason d: the value of a mapping property must be an external term in prefix notation whose prefix is a Prefixes row

validation_hints: Check only schemas whose standard version (own or withStandard) is 8.5.0 or later; unpartnered libraries are not checked
The Sources, Prefixes, and External annotations rows of a partnered library's standard schema count as the library's own
Only dc:source values are checked against the Sources section
specification_reference: A.1.4.2. annotation; A.1.6. Schema sources; Appendix B SCHEMA_ANNOTATION_INVALID

name: attribute-invalid-any-units-not-empty
description: The pseudo unit class anyUnits lists a unit or has defaultUnits.
common_causes: Adding units under anyUnits as if it were an ordinary unit class
Giving anyUnits a defaultUnits attribute
explanation: anyUnits (specification 4.0.0, section 3.1.4.4) is a pseudo unit class: a placeholder with unitClass=anyUnits accepts a value with or without a unit, and any unit of any unit class of the schema. The class itself must list no units and must have no defaultUnits: a value without a unit on such a placeholder is valid but has no default unit and no conversion.
correction_strategy: Keep anyUnits empty; put real units in their own unit classes

correction_examples.explanation: anyUnits lists no units
anyUnits has no default

correction_patterns: anyUnits is empty
No defaultUnits on anyUnits
fix_instructions: 1. Remove any unit lines under anyUnits
2. Remove any defaultUnits attribute from anyUnits
validation_hints: Applies to any schema that defines a unit class named anyUnits

name: library-invalid-reserved-in-unmerged
description: The reserved attribute cannot be used in an unmerged partnered library schema.
common_causes: Marking a partnered library node reserved instead of proposing the reserved tag for the standard schema
Copying a reserved node from the standard schema into a library
explanation: The reserved attribute marks the reserved tags of the standard schema, whose meanings and validation rules are fixed by the HED specification, and can appear only in standard schemas. No library schema may use it on its own elements; this case is the unmerged partnered form (see library-invalid-reserved-in-unpartnered and library-invalid-reserved-in-merged-library-node for the others). The passing companion is the same unmerged library without the attribute.
correction_strategy: Remove the reserved attribute from the library node; reserved tags belong only to the standard schema. If the tag needs a meaning fixed by the specification, propose it for the standard schema instead.

correction_examples.explanation: A partnered library node cannot be reserved; drop the attribute or move the tag to the standard schema.

name: library-invalid-reserved-in-unpartnered
description: An unpartnered library schema cannot use the reserved attribute on its own tags.
common_causes: Marking a library tag reserved to give it special handling by tools
Copying a reserved tag and its attributes from the standard schema into an unpartnered library
explanation: The reserved attribute marks the reserved tags of the standard schema, whose meaning and validation rules are fixed by the HED specification. No library schema, partnered or unpartnered, may put it on its own elements. An unpartnered library has no standard partner, so it has no reserved tags at all, and annotations drawn only from it contain none. Declaring a schema attribute named reserved is not the error here; using it on a tag is. The passing companion declares the attribute but uses it nowhere.
correction_strategy: Remove the reserved attribute from the library's tag. If the tag needs a meaning fixed by the specification, propose it for the standard schema instead.

correction_examples.explanation: Library tags are never reserved; only the standard schema's reserved tags are.

name: library-invalid-reserved-in-merged-library-node
description: In a merged partnered library schema, a library node (one with inLibrary) cannot carry the reserved attribute.
common_causes: Adding reserved to a library node after merging, or before merging in a tool that keeps it
Editing a merged library file by hand instead of the unmerged source
explanation: A merged partnered library schema contains its standard partner's elements, which may carry reserved, and the library's own elements, which carry inLibrary. Only the partner's reserved tags are reserved; a library element with inLibrary must not have the reserved attribute. The passing companion is the same merged schema with reserved removed from the library node.
correction_strategy: Remove the reserved attribute from every element that has inLibrary, and fix the unmerged source so that the next merge does not reintroduce it.

correction_examples.explanation: In a merged file, reserved may appear only on the partner's elements, those without inLibrary.

name: library-invalid-reserved-name
description: A library schema cannot define a tag whose name is a reserved tag of a standard schema, such as Onset.
common_causes: Reusing a familiar name such as Onset, Duration, or Task for a library concept
Copying a reserved tag from the standard schema into an unpartnered library so that it is available without a partner
explanation: The reserved tags (Definition, Def, Def-expand, Onset, Offset, Inset, Delay, Duration, Event-context and the ten organizational tags such as Task and Event-stream) have meanings and validation rules fixed by the specification. A library schema must not define a tag with one of these names, at any level of its hierarchy, even without the reserved attribute: annotations would otherwise contain a tag that looks reserved but is not. For an unmerged partnered library the same tag is also a duplicate of its partner (reason i); this case uses an unpartnered library, where only this rule applies. The passing companion gives the library tag a name of its own.
correction_strategy: Rename the library tag so that its name is not a reserved tag name. If the library needs the reserved tag itself, partner the library with a standard schema and use the partner's tag.

correction_examples.explanation: A library-specific name avoids the reserved name.
The rule applies to every tag the library defines, not only top-level ones.

name: library-invalid-rooted-under-reserved
description: A partnered library schema cannot use rooted to place a node under a reserved tag such as Onset.
common_causes: Rooting a library subtree under Onset or Duration to refine temporal markers
Rooting library task or condition names under Task or Condition-variable instead of using their # value
explanation: A reserved tag has no child node other than #, and a library cannot change that: in the merged schema, a node rooted under a reserved tag would become its child. The rule covers all nineteen reserved tags, including Event-context and the organizational ones such as Task; a reserved tag with a # child would also give that # a sibling. Rooting under an ordinary tag, even the parent of a reserved tag such as Temporal-marker, is allowed.
correction_strategy: Root the library node under an ordinary standard tag, for example the reserved tag's parent, or use the reserved tag's # value where it has one.

correction_examples.explanation: The node becomes a sibling of Onset instead of its child.
Event-context is reserved even though it takes no value; root the node under an ordinary tag.

name: schema-missing-extra
description: An extras section (Sources, Prefixes, or External annotations) has a row with an empty column value.
common_causes: A required column of an extras row was left empty when the row was added
A row was copied from a template and not all columns were filled in
The value was accidentally deleted while editing, leaving 'key=' with nothing after it
A placeholder row was committed before its real values were known
explanation: The extras sections of a HED schema (Sources, Prefixes, and External annotations) are tables in which every row must give a non-empty value in every column: source, link, and description in Sources; prefix, namespace, and description in Prefixes; prefix, id, iri, and description in External annotations. A row that supplies a column key but leaves its value empty (for example 'source=' or 'namespace=') is incomplete, and schema loading reports this warning. The sections themselves are optional in the file: a schema without them is loaded with empty extras sections, and their absence is not an error.
correction_strategy: Fill in every empty column of the flagged extras row, or delete the row entirely if there is no value to record

correction_examples.explanation: The 'source' column of a Sources row was empty; the source name was filled in
The 'namespace' column of a Prefixes row was empty; the ontology namespace was filled in
The 'id' column of an External annotations row was empty; the annotation id was filled in
The 'link' column of a Sources row was empty; every column of an extras row must have a value, not only the key column

specification_reference: 3.1.4.10. Optional extra sections; Appendix B SCHEMA_MISSING_EXTRA

name: schema-reserved-invalid-missing-or-unmarked
description: A standard schema must define every reserved tag with the attributes the reserved-tag rules rely on.
common_causes: Deleting or renaming a reserved tag while editing the standard schema
Dropping reserved or topLevelTagGroup from a reserved tag's attribute list
Adding a new reserved tag to reserved_tags.json without updating the schema, or the reverse
explanation: A standard schema must define every tag that reserved_tags.json names (Definition, Delay, Duration, Event-context, Inset, Offset, Onset, and the valueForms tags Def and Def-expand) together with the attributes the validation rules rely on: reserved on every one of them from 8.2.0, topLevelTagGroup on Delay and Duration from 8.2.0, and from 8.3.0 reserved on the ten organizational reserved tags (Collection, Condition-variable, Control-variable, Event-stream, Experimental-intertrial, Experimental-trial, Indicator-variable, Recording, Task, Time-block). correction_strategy: Restore the missing tag or attribute from the previous release of the standard schema; a reserved tag is never removed or stripped of reserved without a matching change to the specification and reserved_tags.json.

correction_examples.explanation: Every reserved tag carries reserved in standard schemas from 8.2.0.
Delay and Duration need topLevelTagGroup from 8.2.0.
The ten organizational reserved tags must all be present, with reserved, from 8.3.0.
Def and Def-expand need reserved too.

The HED standard schema is a hierarchically-organized vocabulary for annotating events and experimental structure. HED annotations consist of comma-separated tags drawn from this vocabulary. This vocabulary can be augmented by terms drawn from specialized library schema.

The HED standard schema is a hierarchically-organized vocabulary for annotating events and experimental structure. HED annotations consist of comma-separated tags drawn from this vocabulary. This vocabulary can be augmented by terms drawn from specialized library schema.

Each term in this vocabulary has a human-readable description and may include additional attributes that give additional properties or that specify how tools should treat the tag during analysis. The meaning of these attributes is described in the Additional schema properties section.

The HED standard schema is a hierarchically-organized vocabulary for annotating events and experimental structure. HED annotations consist of comma-separated tags drawn from this vocabulary. This vocabulary can be augmented by terms drawn from specialized library schema.

Each term in this vocabulary has a human-readable description and may include additional attributes that give additional properties or that specify how tools should treat the tag during analysis. The meaning of these attributes is described in the Additional schema properties section.

passes: The HED standard schema is a hierarchically-organized vocabulary for annotating events and experimental structure. HED annotations consist of comma-separated tags drawn from this vocabulary. This vocabulary can be augmented by terms drawn from specialized library schema.

Each term in this vocabulary has a human-readable description and may include additional attributes that give additional properties or that specify how tools should treat the tag during analysis. The meaning of these attributes is described in the Additional schema properties section.
'''Item''' <nowiki>{extensionAllowed, hedId=HED_0012171} [An independently existing thing (living or nonliving).]</nowiki>
* Biological-item <nowiki>{hedId=HED_0012172} [An entity that is biological, that is related to living organisms.]</nowiki>
** Anatomical-item <nowiki>{hedId=HED_0012173} [A biological structure, system, fluid or other substance excluding single molecular entities.]</nowiki>
*** Body <nowiki>{hedId=HED_0012174} [The biological structure representing an organism.]</nowiki>

'''Property''' <nowiki>{extensionAllowed, hedId=HED_0012412} [Something that pertains to a thing. A characteristic of some entity. A quality or feature regarded as a characteristic or inherent part of someone or something. HED attributes are adjectives or adverbs.]</nowiki>
* Data-property <nowiki>{extensionAllowed, hedId=HED_0012492} [Something that pertains to data or information.]</nowiki>
** Data-marker <nowiki>{hedId=HED_0012521} [An indicator placed to mark something.]</nowiki>
*** Temporal-marker <nowiki>{hedId=HED_0012523} [An indicator placed at a particular time in the data.]</nowiki>
**** Inset <nowiki>{topLevelTagGroup, reserved, relatedTag=Onset, relatedTag=Offset, hedId=HED_0012524} [Marks an intermediate point in an ongoing event of temporal extent.]</nowiki>
**** Offset <nowiki>{topLevelTagGroup, reserved, relatedTag=Onset, relatedTag=Inset, hedId=HED_0012525} [Marks the end of an event of temporal extent.]</nowiki>
**** Onset <nowiki>{topLevelTagGroup, reserved, relatedTag=Inset, relatedTag=Offset, hedId=HED_0012526} [Marks the start of an ongoing event of temporal extent.]</nowiki>
**** Pause <nowiki>{hedId=HED_0012527} [Indicates the temporary interruption of the operation of a process and subsequently a wait for a signal to continue.]</nowiki>
** Data-value <nowiki>{hedId=HED_0012549} [Designation of the type of a data item.]</nowiki>
*** Spatiotemporal-value <nowiki>{hedId=HED_0012643} [A property relating to space and/or time.]</nowiki>
**** Temporal-value <nowiki>{hedId=HED_0012688} [A characteristic of or relating to time or limited by time.]</nowiki>

***** Delay <nowiki>{topLevelTagGroup, reserved, requireChild, relatedTag=Duration, hedId=HED_0012689} [The time at which an event start time is delayed from the current onset time. This tag defines the start time of an event of temporal extent and may be used with the Duration tag.]</nowiki>

***** Duration <nowiki>{topLevelTagGroup, reserved, requireChild, relatedTag=Delay, hedId=HED_0012691} [The period of time during which an event occurs. This tag defines the end time of an event of temporal extent and may be used with the Delay tag.]</nowiki>
***** Time-interval <nowiki>{hedId=HED_0012693} [The period of time separating two instances, events, or occurrences.]</nowiki>
* Organizational-property <nowiki>{hedId=HED_0012797} [Relating to an organization or the action of organizing something.]</nowiki>
** Collection <nowiki>{reserved, hedId=HED_0012798} [A tag designating a grouping of items such as in a set or list.]</nowiki>

** Condition-variable <nowiki>{reserved, hedId=HED_0012800} [An aspect of the experiment or task that is to be varied during the experiment. Task-conditions are sometimes called independent variables or contrasts.]</nowiki>
***  <nowiki># {takesValue, valueClass=nameClass, hedId=HED_0012801} [Name of the condition variable.]</nowiki>
** Control-variable <nowiki>{reserved, hedId=HED_0012802} [An aspect of the experiment that is fixed throughout the study and usually is explicitly controlled.]</nowiki>
***  <nowiki># {takesValue, valueClass=nameClass, hedId=HED_0012803} [Name of the control variable.]</nowiki>
** Def <nowiki>{requireChild, reserved, hedId=HED_0012804} [A HED-specific utility tag used with a defined name to represent the tags associated with that definition.]</nowiki>

** Def-expand <nowiki>{requireChild, reserved, tagGroup, hedId=HED_0012806} [A HED specific utility tag that is grouped with an expanded definition. The child value of the Def-expand is the name of the expanded definition.]</nowiki>

** Definition <nowiki>{requireChild, reserved, topLevelTagGroup, hedId=HED_0012808} [A HED-specific utility tag whose child value is the name of the concept and the tag group associated with the tag is an English language explanation of a concept.]</nowiki>

** Event-context <nowiki>{reserved, topLevelTagGroup, unique, hedId=HED_0012810} [A special HED tag inserted as part of a top-level tag group to contain information about the interrelated conditions under which the event occurs. The event context includes information about other events that are ongoing when this event happens.]</nowiki>
** Event-stream <nowiki>{reserved, hedId=HED_0012811} [A special HED tag indicating that this event is a member of an ordered succession of events.]</nowiki>
***  <nowiki># {takesValue, valueClass=nameClass, hedId=HED_0012812} [Name of the event stream.]</nowiki>
** Experimental-intertrial <nowiki>{reserved, hedId=HED_0012813} [A tag used to indicate a part of the experiment between trials usually where nothing is happening.]</nowiki>
***  <nowiki># {takesValue, valueClass=nameClass, hedId=HED_0012814} [Optional label for the intertrial block.]</nowiki>

** Experimental-trial <nowiki>{reserved, hedId=HED_0012815} [Designates a run or execution of an activity, for example, one execution of a script. A tag used to indicate a particular organizational part in the experimental design often containing a stimulus-response pair or stimulus-response-feedback triad.]</nowiki>
***  <nowiki># {takesValue, valueClass=nameClass, hedId=HED_0012816} [Optional label for the trial (often a numerical string).]</nowiki>

** Indicator-variable <nowiki>{reserved, hedId=HED_0012817} [An aspect of the experiment or task that is measured as task conditions are varied during the experiment. Experiment indicators are sometimes called dependent variables.]</nowiki>
***  <nowiki># {takesValue, valueClass=nameClass, hedId=HED_0012818} [Name of the indicator variable.]</nowiki>
** Recording <nowiki>{reserved, hedId=HED_0012819} [A tag designating the data recording. Recording tags are usually have temporal scope which is the entire recording.]</nowiki>
***  <nowiki># {takesValue, valueClass=nameClass, hedId=HED_0012820} [Optional label for the recording.]</nowiki>

** Task <nowiki>{reserved, hedId=HED_0012821} [An assigned piece of work, usually with a time allotment. A tag used to indicate a linkage the structured activities performed as part of the experiment.]</nowiki>
***  <nowiki># {takesValue, valueClass=nameClass, hedId=HED_0012822} [Optional label for the task block.]</nowiki>
** Time-block <nowiki>{reserved, hedId=HED_0012823} [A tag used to indicate a contiguous time block in the experiment during which something is fixed or noted.]</nowiki>
***  <nowiki># {takesValue, valueClass=nameClass, hedId=HED_0012824} [Optional label for the task block.]</nowiki>

name: schema-reserved-invalid-child-node
description: A reserved tag in a standard schema cannot have a child node other than #.
common_causes: Adding a refinement such as Onset/Stimulus-onset under a reserved tag
Moving an ordinary tag under a reserved tag while reorganizing the schema
explanation: The reserved tags must not be extended in annotations, and the schema must not give them children either: a reserved tag either takes a value through a # child or has no child at all. Onset has no # child, so any child node fails. The fixtures are the same trimmed copy of 8.5.0 with version 99.0.0 as schema-reserved-invalid-missing-or-unmarked; the passing schema is that copy unchanged, in which Delay, Duration, Def, Def-expand, Definition and most organizational tags have their # child.
correction_strategy: Move the child node elsewhere in the hierarchy, for example beside the reserved tag under its parent.

correction_examples.correct: **** Blah as a sibling of Onset under Temporal-marker
correction_examples.explanation: Only # may be a child of a reserved tag.

passes: The HED standard schema is a hierarchically-organized vocabulary for annotating events and experimental structure. HED annotations consist of comma-separated tags drawn from this vocabulary. This vocabulary can be augmented by terms drawn from specialized library schema.

Each term in this vocabulary has a human-readable description and may include additional attributes that give additional properties or that specify how tools should treat the tag during analysis. The meaning of these attributes is described in the Additional schema properties section.
'''Item''' <nowiki>{extensionAllowed, hedId=HED_0012171} [An independently existing thing (living or nonliving).]</nowiki>
* Biological-item <nowiki>{hedId=HED_0012172} [An entity that is biological, that is related to living organisms.]</nowiki>
** Anatomical-item <nowiki>{hedId=HED_0012173} [A biological structure, system, fluid or other substance excluding single molecular entities.]</nowiki>
*** Body <nowiki>{hedId=HED_0012174} [The biological structure representing an organism.]</nowiki>

'''Property''' <nowiki>{extensionAllowed, hedId=HED_0012412} [Something that pertains to a thing. A characteristic of some entity. A quality or feature regarded as a characteristic or inherent part of someone or something. HED attributes are adjectives or adverbs.]</nowiki>
* Data-property <nowiki>{extensionAllowed, hedId=HED_0012492} [Something that pertains to data or information.]</nowiki>
** Data-marker <nowiki>{hedId=HED_0012521} [An indicator placed to mark something.]</nowiki>
*** Temporal-marker <nowiki>{hedId=HED_0012523} [An indicator placed at a particular time in the data.]</nowiki>
**** Inset <nowiki>{topLevelTagGroup, reserved, relatedTag=Onset, relatedTag=Offset, hedId=HED_0012524} [Marks an intermediate point in an ongoing event of temporal extent.]</nowiki>
**** Offset <nowiki>{topLevelTagGroup, reserved, relatedTag=Onset, relatedTag=Inset, hedId=HED_0012525} [Marks the end of an event of temporal extent.]</nowiki>
**** Onset <nowiki>{topLevelTagGroup, reserved, relatedTag=Inset, relatedTag=Offset, hedId=HED_0012526} [Marks the start of an ongoing event of temporal extent.]</nowiki>
**** Pause <nowiki>{hedId=HED_0012527} [Indicates the temporary interruption of the operation of a process and subsequently a wait for a signal to continue.]</nowiki>
** Data-value <nowiki>{hedId=HED_0012549} [Designation of the type of a data item.]</nowiki>
*** Spatiotemporal-value <nowiki>{hedId=HED_0012643} [A property relating to space and/or time.]</nowiki>
**** Temporal-value <nowiki>{hedId=HED_0012688} [A characteristic of or relating to time or limited by time.]</nowiki>

***** Delay <nowiki>{topLevelTagGroup, reserved, requireChild, relatedTag=Duration, hedId=HED_0012689} [The time at which an event start time is delayed from the current onset time. This tag defines the start time of an event of temporal extent and may be used with the Duration tag.]</nowiki>

***** Duration <nowiki>{topLevelTagGroup, reserved, requireChild, relatedTag=Delay, hedId=HED_0012691} [The period of time during which an event occurs. This tag defines the end time of an event of temporal extent and may be used with the Delay tag.]</nowiki>
***** Time-interval <nowiki>{hedId=HED_0012693} [The period of time separating two instances, events, or occurrences.]</nowiki>
* Organizational-property <nowiki>{hedId=HED_0012797} [Relating to an organization or the action of organizing something.]</nowiki>
** Collection <nowiki>{reserved, hedId=HED_0012798} [A tag designating a grouping of items such as in a set or list.]</nowiki>

** Condition-variable <nowiki>{reserved, hedId=HED_0012800} [An aspect of the experiment or task that is to be varied during the experiment. Task-conditions are sometimes called independent variables or contrasts.]</nowiki>
***  <nowiki># {takesValue, valueClass=nameClass, hedId=HED_0012801} [Name of the condition variable.]</nowiki>
** Control-variable <nowiki>{reserved, hedId=HED_0012802} [An aspect of the experiment that is fixed throughout the study and usually is explicitly controlled.]</nowiki>
***  <nowiki># {takesValue, valueClass=nameClass, hedId=HED_0012803} [Name of the control variable.]</nowiki>
** Def <nowiki>{requireChild, reserved, hedId=HED_0012804} [A HED-specific utility tag used with a defined name to represent the tags associated with that definition.]</nowiki>

** Def-expand <nowiki>{requireChild, reserved, tagGroup, hedId=HED_0012806} [A HED specific utility tag that is grouped with an expanded definition. The child value of the Def-expand is the name of the expanded definition.]</nowiki>

** Definition <nowiki>{requireChild, reserved, topLevelTagGroup, hedId=HED_0012808} [A HED-specific utility tag whose child value is the name of the concept and the tag group associated with the tag is an English language explanation of a concept.]</nowiki>

** Event-context <nowiki>{reserved, topLevelTagGroup, unique, hedId=HED_0012810} [A special HED tag inserted as part of a top-level tag group to contain information about the interrelated conditions under which the event occurs. The event context includes information about other events that are ongoing when this event happens.]</nowiki>
** Event-stream <nowiki>{reserved, hedId=HED_0012811} [A special HED tag indicating that this event is a member of an ordered succession of events.]</nowiki>
***  <nowiki># {takesValue, valueClass=nameClass, hedId=HED_0012812} [Name of the event stream.]</nowiki>
** Experimental-intertrial <nowiki>{reserved, hedId=HED_0012813} [A tag used to indicate a part of the experiment between trials usually where nothing is happening.]</nowiki>
***  <nowiki># {takesValue, valueClass=nameClass, hedId=HED_0012814} [Optional label for the intertrial block.]</nowiki>

** Experimental-trial <nowiki>{reserved, hedId=HED_0012815} [Designates a run or execution of an activity, for example, one execution of a script. A tag used to indicate a particular organizational part in the experimental design often containing a stimulus-response pair or stimulus-response-feedback triad.]</nowiki>
***  <nowiki># {takesValue, valueClass=nameClass, hedId=HED_0012816} [Optional label for the trial (often a numerical string).]</nowiki>

** Indicator-variable <nowiki>{reserved, hedId=HED_0012817} [An aspect of the experiment or task that is measured as task conditions are varied during the experiment. Experiment indicators are sometimes called dependent variables.]</nowiki>
***  <nowiki># {takesValue, valueClass=nameClass, hedId=HED_0012818} [Name of the indicator variable.]</nowiki>
** Recording <nowiki>{reserved, hedId=HED_0012819} [A tag designating the data recording. Recording tags are usually have temporal scope which is the entire recording.]</nowiki>
***  <nowiki># {takesValue, valueClass=nameClass, hedId=HED_0012820} [Optional label for the recording.]</nowiki>

** Task <nowiki>{reserved, hedId=HED_0012821} [An assigned piece of work, usually with a time allotment. A tag used to indicate a linkage the structured activities performed as part of the experiment.]</nowiki>
***  <nowiki># {takesValue, valueClass=nameClass, hedId=HED_0012822} [Optional label for the task block.]</nowiki>
** Time-block <nowiki>{reserved, hedId=HED_0012823} [A tag used to indicate a contiguous time block in the experiment during which something is fixed or noted.]</nowiki>
***  <nowiki># {takesValue, valueClass=nameClass, hedId=HED_0012824} [Optional label for the task block.]</nowiki>

name: schema-section-missing
description: A required schema section is missing from the schema file.
common_causes: Missing required schema sections
Sections not in correct order
Incorrect section markers or delimiters
Incomplete schema template usage
Copy-paste errors in schema creation
explanation: HED schemas must contain all required sections in the correct order: Prologue, Schema, Unit classes, Unit modifiers, Value classes, Schema attributes, Properties, and Epilogue. Missing or misplaced sections prevent proper schema validation.
correction_strategy: Add missing sections in correct order with proper delimiters

correction_examples.explanation: Added required section with proper MediaWiki formatting

correction_examples.correct: Reorder to: Prologue, Schema, Unit classes, Unit modifiers, Value classes, Schema attributes, Properties, Epilogue
correction_examples.explanation: Arranged sections in required sequence

correction_patterns: Include all required sections even if empty
Use proper section delimiters (''' for MediaWiki)
Follow exact section ordering requirements
Check section names match required format
Ensure proper start/end schema markers
fix_instructions: 1. Check for all required sections
2. Verify sections are in correct order
3. Add missing sections with proper delimiters
4. Ensure section names match requirements exactly
5. Validate schema structure completeness
validation_hints: Empty sections are allowed but must be present
Section order is strictly enforced
Use exact section names and formatting
Check both start and end markers
